overview: This 589-page file traces U.S. and Allied oversight of Japanese fisheries and Antarctic whaling during the occupation, chiefly from 1947 to 1949. Diplomatic correspondence, SCAP directives, policy drafts, industry reports, and statistics document disputes over fishing boundaries, conservation, enforcement, whaling fleets, and Allied authority. A concluding weekly summary broadens the record to Japanese agriculture and natural resources.
interest: The file exposes how occupation officials balanced Japan’s food needs against conservation, industry interests, and Allied objections.
